# Privacy and confidential reporting

This public repository distributes course materials. Use this page when a
published file or link appears to expose information that should remain
private, or when a concern needs confidential handling.

Examples include personal information in a document or screenshot, grades or
feedback, an unreleased student submission, instructor-marked private material,
or an exposed password or access token.

## Report the location privately

Email Prof. Gabriel Spadon at [spadon@dal.ca](mailto:spadon@dal.ca). Enrolled
students should use their Dalhousie email. Provide enough information to locate
the concern without creating another copy of the sensitive material.

- Give the file or page URL and the relevant page, slide, or location.
- Briefly describe the type of information exposed and why it appears private.
- Say when you noticed it, especially if a link or file has since changed.

Do not include passwords, access tokens, entire private submissions, or
unredacted personal records in the report. Do not post the concern in a public
issue, pull request, portfolio, or class-wide Teams message. A private email
allows the location to be checked without spreading the information further.

## Limit further exposure

Do not repost, redistribute, or test any exposed credentials. Share the location
with the instructor rather than forwarding the file to classmates. If the
exposure is in your own repository or cloud notebook, restrict its sharing
while preserving the recorded assessment history and contact the instructor.

If private information was committed accidentally, follow the syllabus process
for an approved correction. Do not amend, rebase, squash, delete, replace, or
force-push recorded assessment commits on your own. The submitted SHA and the
instructor-retained snapshot must remain an independent reference for the
assessment.

## Public materials and private information

Instructor-released course materials may be shared with credit unless they are
explicitly marked private or restricted. Keep third-party attributions and
applicable licence terms. This permission does not authorize sharing another
student's work, grades, feedback, personal information, or unreleased recordings.

Your own assessed work remains private until the deadline has passed and the
instructor opens sharing. The [syllabus](../assets/planning/syllabus.pdf)
governs privacy, portfolio release, and approved alternatives when public
sharing is unsuitable.

For a typo, broken public link, or an error in an example that does not expose
private information, use the
[course-material correction guidance](CONTRIBUTING.md).
